requirements.subject: ent:value
requirements.canonical: A value used in an assignment, an instantiation or a comparison SHALL be type compatible with the type of the target or of the other operand.
requirements.original: Generally, TTCN-3 requires type compatibility of values at assignments, instantiations and comparison.

ambiguity.issue: 'Generally' implies exceptions without listing them here; the exceptions (strong typing) are given in clause 6.3.4. Chose the reading that type compatibility is the default rule.
readings: A value used in an assignment, an instantiation or a comparison SHALL be type compatible with the target type, except where clause 6.3.4 requires strong typing.
A value used in an assignment, an instantiation or a comparison SHALL be type compatible with the target type in all cases.

requirements.subject: ent:value-b
requirements.canonical: Value "b" IS the actual value that is assigned, passed as parameter, etc., in the type compatibility rules of clause 6.3.
requirements.original: For the purpose of this clause the actual value to be assigned, passed as parameter, etc. is called value "b".

requirements.subject: ent:type-b
requirements.canonical: Type "B" IS the type of value "b" in the type compatibility rules of clause 6.3.
requirements.original: The type of value "b" is called type "B".

requirements.subject: ent:type-a
requirements.canonical: Type "A" IS the type of the object (formal parameter, variable, etc.) that obtains value "b" in the type compatibility rules of clause 6.3.
requirements.original: The type of the formal parameter, which is to obtain the actual value of value "b" is called type "A".

ambiguity.issue: Type "A" is defined only as the type of a formal parameter, but the rules of clause 6.3 also apply to assignments and comparisons. Chose the wider reading.
readings: Type "A" IS the type of the object (formal parameter, variable, etc.) that obtains value "b".
Type "A" IS only the type of the formal parameter that obtains value "b".

improper_terms.proper: target object (formal parameter, variable, template variable, field)

requirements.subject: ent:address-type
requirements.canonical: An `address` type and its derivatives ARE subject to the same type compatibility rules as a type with the same definition but a name different from `address`.
requirements.original: NOTE: As address is more a predefined type name than a distinct type with its own properties, the same type compatibility rules apply to an address type and to its derivatives as the rules were if the type was defined with a name different from address.

requirements.subject: ent:value-b
requirements.condition: type "B" is a simple basic type or basic string type
requirements.canonical: A value "b" of a simple basic type or basic string type IS compatible with type "A" if type "B" resolves to the same root type as type "A" and value "b" does not violate the subtyping (e.g. ranges, length restrictions) of type "A".
requirements.original: For variables, constants, templates, etc. of simple basic types and basic string types the value "b" is compatible to type "A" if type "B" resolves to the same root type as type "A" (e.g. integer) and it does not violate subtyping (e.g. ranges, length restrictions) of type "A".

requirements.subject: ent:charstring-type
requirements.canonical: A value "b" of charstring type IS compatible with a universal charstring type "A" unless value "b" violates a type constraint specification (range, list or length) of type "A".
requirements.original: For variables, constants, templates, etc. of charstring type, value 'b' is compatible with a universal charstring type 'A' unless it violates any type constraint specification (range, list or length) of type "A".

ambiguity.issue: The source unit is classified as example-text by the sentence splitter, but in the spec it is normative prose that follows the examples.

requirements.subject: ent:universal-charstring-type
requirements.canonical: A value "b" of universal charstring type IS compatible with a charstring type "A" if every character of value "b" has a corresponding character (the same control or graphical character with the same character code) in the charstring type and value "b" does not violate a type constraint specification (range, list or length) of type "A".
requirements.original: For variables, constants, templates, etc. of universal charstring type, value 'b' is compatible with a charstring type 'A' if all characters used in value 'b' have their corresponding characters (i.e. the same control or graphical character using the same character code) in the type charstring and it does not violate any type constraint specification (range, list or length) of type "A".

ambiguity.issue: The source unit is classified as example-text by the sentence splitter, but in the spec it is normative prose that follows the examples.

requirements.subject: ent:value-b
requirements.canonical: In clause 6.3.2, value "b" IS the value to be assigned (e.g. passed as parameter) to an object of type "A".
requirements.original: In subsequent clauses, "value "b"" is called the value to be assigned, e.g. when passed as parameter, to an object of type "A".

requirements.subject: ent:enumerated-type
requirements.canonical: An enumerated type IS NOT compatible with any type other than an enumerated type.
requirements.original: Enumerated types are only compatible with other enumerated types.

requirements.subject: ent:enumerated-value
requirements.canonical: An enumerated value "b" of an enumerated type "B" IS compatible with an enumerated type "A" if the identifier of value "b" is also defined in type "A" and the integer value(s) associated with value "b" are associated with the same identifier in type "A".
requirements.original: An enumerated value "b" of an enumerated type "B" is compatible with enumerated type "A" if the identifier of the value "b" is also defined in "A" and the integer(s) associated with value "b" are also associated with the same identifier in "A".

requirements.subject: ent:record-type
requirements.canonical: A value "b" of record type "B" IS compatible with record type "A" if the number and the optionality of the fields in textual order of definition are identical, the types of corresponding fields are compatible, and the value of each present field of value "b" is compatible with the type of the corresponding field in type "A".
requirements.original: record types are compatible if the number, and optional aspect of the fields in the textual order of definition are identical, the types of each field are compatible and the value of each existing field of the value "b" is compatible with the type of its corresponding field in type "A".

ambiguity.issue: 'the types of each field are compatible' does not say whether field types need only the same root type or must be compatible including subtyping; EXAMPLE 1 accepts AType (field a(0..10)) and BType (field a integer), so the root-type reading was chosen. Field names are irrelevant (EXAMPLE 1, CType).
readings: Corresponding field types SHALL resolve to the same root type; subtype violations are checked on the field values of value "b".
Corresponding field types SHALL be compatible including their subtype constraints.

requirements.subject: ent:value-b
requirements.canonical: When a value "b" of a record type is assigned to an object of a compatible record type "A", the value of each field of value "b" IS assigned to the positionally corresponding field of the value of type "A".
requirements.original: The value of each field in the value "b" is assigned to the corresponding field in the value of type "A".

requirements.subject: ent:record-of-type
requirements.canonical: A value "b" of a `record of` type or array type IS compatible with a `record of` type or array type "A" if the element types are compatible and value "b" does not violate any length subtyping of the `record of` type "A" or the dimensions of the array type "A".
requirements.original: `record of` types and arrays are compatible if their element types are compatible and value "b" does not violate any length subtyping of the `record of` type "A" or dimensions of the array type.

ambiguity.issue: The source unit is classified as example-text by the sentence splitter, but in the spec it is normative prose that follows the examples. Kept normative=false only because no normative unit of this part can serve as source.

requirements.subject: ent:value-b
requirements.canonical: When a value "b" of a `record of` or array type is assigned to an instance of type "A", the element values of value "b" SHALL be assigned sequentially to the instance of type "A", including undefined elements.
requirements.original: Values of elements of the value "b" shall be assigned sequentially to the instance of type "A", including undefined elements.

ambiguity.issue: The source unit is classified as example-text by the sentence splitter, but in the spec it is normative prose that follows the examples.

requirements.subject: ent:array
requirements.canonical: An array type IS compatible with another array type if their corresponding `record of` types are compatible.
requirements.original: Two array types are compatible if their corresponding `record of` types are compatible.

ambiguity.issue: The source unit is classified as example-text by the sentence splitter, but in the spec it is normative prose that follows the examples.
